case_title: Chhangar @ Manoj v. State of M. P.
aggravating_circumstances: Use of lethal weapons, exhortation to commit murder, motive of killing as an informer
mitigating_circumstances: Nature of injuries was simple due to bomb explosion at a distance
trial_court_outcome: Convicted and sentenced to three years imprisonment
neutral_facts: The accused, along with three other individuals, were involved in an incident where one of the accused hurled two bombs at the victim, who was sitting in a bettel shop. The bombs exploded, causing injury to the victim's left thigh. The accused in question, referred to as the appellant, was present at the scene and reportedly shouted words indicating an intent to kill the victim, who was an informer. The victim's brother was the informant. The prosecution relied on the testimony of the injured eye-witness, corroborated by other witnesses, to establish the common intention among the accused to commit the act. The accused were found guilty of attempting to murder the victim, and the trial court sentenced them to three years of imprisonment.
